title: XはYです — "X is Y"
explanation:
The most basic sentence pattern in Japanese. は (wa) marks the topic of the sentence, and です (desu) is the polite copula meaning 'is/am/are'. This is used to identify or describe the topic.

**Key Point:** は is written with the hiragana は but pronounced 'wa' when used as a particle.
examples: [{"japanese":"わたしはがくせいです。","english":"I am a student.","notes":"Basic self-introduction"},{"japanese":"たなかさんはにほんじんです。","english":"Tanaka is Japanese.","notes":"Describing someone's nationality"},{"japanese":"これはほんです。","english":"This is a book.","notes":"Identifying an object"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you say 'I am a teacher' in Japanese?","options":["わたしはせんせいです。","わたしはがくせいです。","せんせいはわたしです。","わたしのせんせいです。"],"answer":"わたしはせんせいです。"},{"type":"quiz","question":"What does 'メアリーさんはアメリカじんです' mean?","options":["Mary is American.","Mary likes America.","Mary went to America.","Mary is in America."],"answer":"Mary is American."}]

title: XはYじゃないです — Negative
explanation:
To make a negative sentence with です, replace です with じゃないです (informal) or ではありません (formal). Both mean 'is not'.

**Note:** じゃないです is more commonly used in everyday conversation. ではありません is more formal/written.
structure: [Topic] は [Description] じゃないです / ではありません
examples: [{"japanese":"わたしはせんせいじゃないです。","english":"I am not a teacher.","notes":"Casual negative"},{"japanese":"これはわたしのかばんではありません。","english":"This is not my bag.","notes":"Formal negative"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you negate 'がくせいです'?","options":["がくせいじゃないです","がくせいません","がくせいないです","がくせいじゃです"],"answer":"がくせいじゃないです"}]

title: XはYですか — Question
explanation:
To form a question in Japanese, simply add か (ka) at the end of a statement. Unlike English, you don't need to change word order.

**Key Point:** In polite speech, the intonation rises at the end of a question, similar to English.
examples: [{"japanese":"がくせいですか。","english":"Are you a student?","notes":"Simple yes/no question"},{"japanese":"たなかさんはにほんじんですか。","english":"Is Tanaka Japanese?","notes":"Asking about someone"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"Turn 'せんせいです' into a question.","options":["せんせいですか。","せんせいですね。","せんせいでしょう。","せんせいですよ。"],"answer":"せんせいですか。"}]

title: の — Possessive Particle
explanation:
The particle の (no) connects two nouns and shows possession or association, similar to 's in English or 'of'.

**Usage:** The order is [Owner] の [Possession], which is opposite to English's 'of' construction.
examples: [{"japanese":"わたしのほんです。","english":"It is my book.","notes":"Possession"},{"japanese":"だいがくのせんせいです。","english":"(He is) a university professor.","notes":"Association"},{"japanese":"にほんごのがくせいです。","english":"(I am) a student of Japanese.","notes":"Describing what kind"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you say 'Tanaka's friend'?","options":["たなかさんのともだち","たなかさんはともだち","たなかさんがともだち","たなかさんをともだち"],"answer":"たなかさんのともだち"}]

title: じかん — Telling Time
explanation:
To tell time in Japanese, use the number + じ (ji) for hours. For minutes, use the number + ぷん/ふん (fun/pun). はん (han) means 'half past'.

**Key Point:** Some numbers change pronunciation when combined with じ: 4時 = よじ, 7時 = しちじ, 9時 = くじ.
examples: [{"japanese":"いまさんじです。","english":"It is 3 o'clock now.","notes":""},{"japanese":"ろくじはんにおきます。","english":"I wake up at 6:30.","notes":"はん = half past"},{"japanese":"なんじですか。","english":"What time is it?","notes":"Asking the time"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you say '9 o'clock'?","options":["くじ","きゅうじ","ここのつじ","きゅじ"],"answer":"くじ"}]

title: Verb ます Form — Polite Present/Future
explanation:
Japanese verbs in polite speech end in ます (masu). This form is used for habitual actions and future plans. The negative is ません (masen).

**Key Point:** ます form doesn't change with the subject — no conjugation for I/you/he/she!
examples: [{"japanese":"コーヒーをのみます。","english":"I drink coffee.","notes":"Habitual action"},{"japanese":"テレビをみません。","english":"I don't watch TV.","notes":"Negative"},{"japanese":"あしたがっこうにいきます。","english":"I will go to school tomorrow.","notes":"Future plan"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"What is the negative of たべます?","options":["たべません","たべないます","たべますない","たべじゃないます"],"answer":"たべません"}]

title: を — Object Marker
explanation:
The particle を (wo, pronounced 'o') marks the direct object of a verb — the thing that receives the action.

**Key Point:** を is only used with transitive verbs (verbs that take an object).
examples: [{"japanese":"ほんをよみます。","english":"I read a book.","notes":"Object + verb"},{"japanese":"みずをのみます。","english":"I drink water.","notes":""},{"japanese":"にほんごをべんきょうします。","english":"I study Japanese.","notes":""}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"Fill in the blank: すし＿たべます。","options":["を","は","に","で"],"answer":"を"}]

title: に — Time/Destination Particle
explanation:
The particle に (ni) has two main uses: (1) marking a specific point in time, and (2) marking the destination/direction of movement.

**Key Point:** Use に with specific times (3 o'clock, Monday) but NOT with relative times (today, tomorrow).
examples: [{"japanese":"しちじにおきます。","english":"I wake up at 7.","notes":"Time marker"},{"japanese":"がっこうにいきます。","english":"I go to school.","notes":"Destination"},{"japanese":"にちようびにえいがをみます。","english":"I watch a movie on Sunday.","notes":"Day of the week"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"Fill in the blank: 三じ＿おきます。","options":["に","を","は","で"],"answer":"に"}]

title: で — Location/Means Particle
explanation:
The particle で (de) marks: (1) the location where an action takes place, and (2) the means/method of doing something.

**Key Point:** で is used for actions at a location, while に indicates existence at a location.
examples: [{"japanese":"としょかんでべんきょうします。","english":"I study at the library.","notes":"Location of action"},{"japanese":"はしでたべます。","english":"I eat with chopsticks.","notes":"Means/instrument"},{"japanese":"バスでいきます。","english":"I go by bus.","notes":"Means of transport"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"Fill in the blank: レストラン＿たべます。","options":["で","に","を","は"],"answer":"で"}]

title: が — Subject Marker & Likes/Dislikes
explanation:
The particle が (ga) marks the subject. It's especially used with: (1) existence verbs (ある/いる), (2) adjectives of desire/ability, (3) expressing likes/dislikes (すき/きらい).

**は vs が:** は marks the topic (what the sentence is about), while が marks the subject (what does the action or exists).
examples: [{"japanese":"ねこがいます。","english":"There is a cat.","notes":"Existence"},{"japanese":"すしがすきです。","english":"I like sushi.","notes":"Likes"},{"japanese":"にほんごがわかります。","english":"I understand Japanese.","notes":"Ability"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"Fill in the blank: コーヒー＿すきです。","options":["が","を","は","に"],"answer":"が"}]

title: ある / いる — Existence
explanation:
Japanese has two verbs for 'to exist': ある (aru) for inanimate objects and いる (iru) for animate beings (people, animals).

**Pattern:** [Place] に [Thing] が あります/います
structure: [Place] に [Subject] が あります / います
examples: [{"japanese":"つくえのうえにほんがあります。","english":"There is a book on the desk.","notes":"Inanimate = ある"},{"japanese":"こうえんにこどもがいます。","english":"There are children in the park.","notes":"Animate = いる"},{"japanese":"にわにねこがいます。","english":"There is a cat in the garden.","notes":"Animals = いる"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"Which verb do you use for a cat?","options":["います","あります"],"answer":"います"}]

title: Verb ました / ませんでした — Past Tense
explanation:
To express past tense in polite form: ます → ました (did) and ません → ませんでした (didn't).

For です: です → でした (was) and じゃないです → じゃなかったです (wasn't).
structure: [Verb stem] ました / ませんでした
examples: [{"japanese":"きのうえいがをみました。","english":"I watched a movie yesterday.","notes":"Past affirmative"},{"japanese":"あさごはんをたべませんでした。","english":"I didn't eat breakfast.","notes":"Past negative"},{"japanese":"きのうはあめでした。","english":"It was rainy yesterday.","notes":"です past = でした"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"What is the past tense of いきます?","options":["いきました","いくました","いきたです","いったです"],"answer":"いきました"}]

title: い-Adjectives — Conjugation
explanation:
い-adjectives end in い and conjugate by dropping the い:
- Present: おおきい (big)
- Negative: おおきくない (not big)
- Past: おおきかった (was big)
- Past Negative: おおきくなかった (wasn't big)

**Exception:** いい (good) conjugates irregularly: よくない, よかった, よくなかった.
structure: Adj-い / Adj-くない / Adj-かった / Adj-くなかった
examples: [{"japanese":"このレストランはたかいです。","english":"This restaurant is expensive.","notes":"Present"},{"japanese":"きょうはさむくないです。","english":"It's not cold today.","notes":"Negative"},{"japanese":"きのうはあつかったです。","english":"It was hot yesterday.","notes":"Past"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"What is the negative of おおきい?","options":["おおきくない","おおきじゃない","おおきない","おおきません"],"answer":"おおきくない"}]

title: な-Adjectives — Conjugation
explanation:
な-adjectives don't end in い (except きれい and ゆうめい). They behave like nouns with です:
- Present: しずかです (quiet)
- Negative: しずかじゃないです (not quiet)
- Past: しずかでした (was quiet)
- Modifying a noun: しずかな + noun
structure: Adj-な + Noun / Adj です / Adj じゃないです
examples: [{"japanese":"ここはしずかです。","english":"This place is quiet.","notes":"Present"},{"japanese":"しずかなへやがすきです。","english":"I like quiet rooms.","notes":"Modifying a noun"},{"japanese":"きれいじゃなかったです。","english":"It wasn't pretty.","notes":"Past negative"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you say 'a quiet park'?","options":["しずかなこうえん","しずかいこうえん","しずかのこうえん","しずかこうえん"],"answer":"しずかなこうえん"}]

title: Te-form (て form) — Connecting & Requesting
explanation:
The て-form is one of the most important verb forms. It's used for:
1. Making requests: ～てください (Please do...)
2. Connecting actions: ～て、～て (do X, then do Y)
3. Ongoing actions: ～ている (is doing)

**Rules for making て-form:**
- う/つ/る → って
- む/ぶ/ぬ → んで
- く → いて (except 行く → 行って)
- ぐ → いで
- す → して
examples: [{"japanese":"すわってください。","english":"Please sit down.","notes":"Request"},{"japanese":"あさおきて、シャワーをあびて、ごはんをたべます。","english":"I wake up, take a shower, and eat.","notes":"Connecting actions"},{"japanese":"いまべんきょうしています。","english":"I am studying now.","notes":"Ongoing action"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"What is the て-form of 食べる?","options":["食べて","食べって","食べんで","食べいて"],"answer":"食べて"}]

title: ～ている — Progressive/State
explanation:
Verb て-form + いる expresses:
1. An ongoing action (progressive): 食べている = is eating
2. A habitual action: 毎日走っている = runs every day
3. A resultant state: 結婚している = is married (result of getting married)

Polite form: ～ています
structure: [Verb て-form] います / いません
examples: [{"japanese":"いまテレビをみています。","english":"I am watching TV now.","notes":"Progressive"},{"japanese":"とうきょうにすんでいます。","english":"I live in Tokyo.","notes":"State"},{"japanese":"たなかさんをしっています。","english":"I know Tanaka.","notes":"Resultant state"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"What does 'すんでいます' mean?","options":["I live (somewhere)","I am swimming","I am sitting","I am sleeping"],"answer":"I live (somewhere)"}]

title: ～たい — Want to Do
explanation:
To express desire to do something, replace ます with たいです. The object can be marked with を or が.

**Note:** ～たい is only used for your own desires. For asking others, use ～たいですか (casual) or ～ませんか (polite invitation).
examples: [{"japanese":"すしをたべたいです。","english":"I want to eat sushi.","notes":""},{"japanese":"にほんにいきたいです。","english":"I want to go to Japan.","notes":""},{"japanese":"のみたくないです。","english":"I don't want to drink.","notes":"Negative"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you say 'I want to read'?","options":["よみたいです","よむたいです","よみたです","よんたいです"],"answer":"よみたいです"}]

title: ～てもいいですか — Permission
explanation: To ask for permission, use the て-form + もいいですか (May I...?). To grant permission: いいですよ (Yes, you may). To refuse: ちょっと... (Well...) or ～てはいけません (You must not).
examples: [{"japanese":"しゃしんをとってもいいですか。","english":"May I take a photo?","notes":"Asking permission"},{"japanese":"いいですよ。","english":"Yes, that's fine.","notes":"Granting permission"},{"japanese":"ここでたべてはいけません。","english":"You must not eat here.","notes":"Prohibition"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you ask 'May I sit here'?","options":["ここにすわってもいいですか。","ここにすわりますか。","ここにすわれますか。","ここにすわりたいですか。"],"answer":"ここにすわってもいいですか。"}]

title: ～ないでください — Negative Request
explanation:
To ask someone NOT to do something, use the negative て-form: ない → ないで + ください.

This is the polite way to say 'Please don't...'.
structure: [Verb ない-form] で ください
examples: [{"japanese":"ここでたばこをすわないでください。","english":"Please don't smoke here.","notes":""},{"japanese":"しんぱいしないでください。","english":"Please don't worry.","notes":""},{"japanese":"わすれないでください。","english":"Please don't forget.","notes":""}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"How do you say 'Please don't run'?","options":["はしらないでください","はしってください","はしりません","はしらないます"],"answer":"はしらないでください"}]

title: から / まで — From / Until
explanation:
から (kara) means 'from' (time/place) and まで (made) means 'until/to' (time/place). They are often used together.

**Note:** から can also mean 'because' when placed after a clause.
examples: [{"japanese":"くじからごじまではたらきます。","english":"I work from 9 to 5.","notes":"Time range"},{"japanese":"とうきょうからおおさかまでしんかんせんでいきます。","english":"I go from Tokyo to Osaka by bullet train.","notes":"Place range"},{"japanese":"あめですから、かさをもっていきます。","english":"Because it's raining, I'll take an umbrella.","notes":"Because"}]
exercises: [{"type":"quiz","question":"Fill in: 8時＿5時＿べんきょうします。","options":["から...まで","に...を","で...に","は...が"],"answer":"から...まで"}]
